item.title: [English · 90s Briefing] From Ephemeral Inference to Compiled Agency
item.description: First, advanced computing becomes affordable for everyone when expensive neural models act as a last resort behind fast local lookup tables, search indexes, and exact solvers. Second, compressing weights below one bit saves memory, yet unpacking them back to floating-point numbers at runtime wastes over eighty times more circuit-board energy than running packed integer logic directly. Third, one integer kernel checked by cryptographic hashes produces the exact same answer across processors, graphics cards, WebAssembly, hardware logic, and microcontrollers, halting immediately if a single weight changes. Across fifteen hundred deterministic control tasks, zero-model lookup beat neural baselines by 61.60 percentage points on structured tool schemas and 20.80 points on Boolean satisfiability at 1.41 to 2.09 microjoules net shunt energy, cleanly isolating the 12.80 point open coding triage gap. On an AMD Kria five-volt board shunt with 0.09 to 0.11 percent idle drift, unpacking 0.1517 bits-per-weight matrices to 32-bit floats burned 63,335.56 microjoules gross—81.86 times worse than eight-bit integers—while packed integer Walsh-Hadamard, exclusive-NOR, bit-count, and nibble lookup dropped to 187.49 microjoules gross and 10.30 microjoules net. One hash-verified integer kernel matched bit-for-bit across ten lanes and six fabrics—processor, Radeon 8060S Vulkan graphics, split processor-graphics, WebAssembly vectors, Verilog hardware logic, and a 1,444-byte bare-metal microcontroller—halting on single-weight tamper alongside 1,315 Planetary Digital Well lowering recipes. End to end, the four-stage spellcheck cascade cut Kria shunt energy 26.58 times gross and 24.49 times net, cut Jetson Thor shunt energy 16.26 times, and avoided 38.46 times of stage-four calls. All receipts are Signed Provenance, Self-Checked—not externally peer-reviewed—with shunt, chip-counter, estimated, and unmetered joules kept strictly separate.

item.title: [English · 90s Briefing] Deterministic Null
item.description: First, most AI benchmarks skip a zero-model control group that tests what simple lookup already solves. Second, on bounded math and database tasks, a frozen lookup table matched cloud AI on nine of ten tests. Third, on open coding tasks AI leaped ahead, while caching verified answers cut repeat energy three point six times. If two hundred-billion-parameter models both score ninety-nine percent on a structured benchmark, did either one actually need a neural network at decision time? Without a zero-model control group on the exact same exam, nobody can tell the difference. We built an eight-step integer lookup table verified bit-for-bit across Rust, Go, Python, Julia, and C plus plus, then anchored its digital fingerprints onto public Bitcoin calendar proofs before public randomness beacons generated four thousand thirty fresh held-out problems. Across two thousand eight hundred forty bounded math and database problems, cloud models beat the frozen table on only unindexed customer phrasing, yet jumped forty-four to ninety-five percentage points ahead across four externally authored software engineering benchmarks. When newly verified neural fixes are written back into the lookup store, realistic skewed workloads cut recurring model calls and local chip energy by three point five nine times.

item.title: [English · 90s Briefing] RCE Compile
item.description: First, real compilers break any single descriptive law, so this study defines a seven-part yardstick instead. Second, maximum compiler optimization burns upfront energy that never pays back on thirty percent of test programs. Third, fingerprinting code by variable position reuses builds with zero mix-ups, cutting Rust compile energy four hundredfold. We tested a sweeping claim—that every compiler lowers canonical forms while tracking energy and preserving meaning—against twelve real compiler families. In practice, none tracks joules, none hashes name-free code, and automated fuzzers have uncovered thousands of C compiler bugs. Restating compilation as a seven-part standard lets us measure exact payback horizons across twenty kernels and fifteen toolchain tiers: optimized C beats Python after twenty-four hundred ninety runs, while shared Rust runtime libraries cut build energy twentyfold. Simply erasing variable names caused one hundred fifty dangerous cache collisions whenever two variables swapped roles. Replacing names with De Bruijn binding positions hit zero false matches across five hundred verified mutants and cut warm C and Rust rebuilds up to four hundred forty-eight times. All energy figures come from built-in Linux processor counters rather than an external wall wattmeter, and every external citation carries an explicit verification badge.

item.title: [English · 90s Briefing] "AI" Reads Human
item.description: First, computers often swap data in text formats written for human eyes, forcing machines to spend extra work. Second, reading indented configuration text took over two thousand times more chip energy than reading compact machine numbers. Third, chopping structured text into AI word pieces burned twelve times more energy than parsing the text itself. Formats full of curly braces, commas, and indented spaces were designed so people could inspect files comfortably in text editors. Yet modern AI tool pipelines pass millions of those verbose text records strictly from machine to machine without a human ever looking. We named this extra work the impedance tax and tested thirty-four parsing and word-splitting workloads across twenty thousand records. Running each pass inside an isolated worker process on an Apple processor cleanly separated tiny parsing costs from noisy background laptop activity. Unpacking a twenty-three-byte binary record used two hundred eighty nanojoules. Standard bracketed text used nearly eight times more, compiled indented text used two hundred forty-nine times more, and pure Python indented text burned two thousand fifty-four times more chip energy. Even adding two spaces of pretty indentation more than doubled AI word-splitting energy to seventy-one microjoules per record. Keep internal machine pipes compact and binary, and format text only when people read.
